title: Probe scheduling and telemetry attenuation checklist
content:
Context:
This is a working checklist for scheduling synthetic probes, attenuating noisy telemetry, and shaping dashboards to reduce operator noise while preserving investigatability for inference-specific failure modes (kv-cache churn, prefix-miss cascades, model fallback loops).

Intent / problem statement:
- Our current probe cadence + full-trace capture is creating too much query/trace cost in high-traffic regions; oncall noise increasing.
- We need a repeatable schedule and attenuation rules that: 
  * keep early-warning signals (warm-start regressions, microburst latency)
  * remove low-signal, high-volume probes from default dashboards
  * maintain trace anchors for postmortem linkability

High-level constraints and goals:
- SLO-first: do not weaken signal required for SLO detection (p95/p99 tail for user-facing routes).
- Query budget: reduce synthetic probe contribution to telemetry cost by ~40% in EU region by Q1 2026.
- Trace storage: only full spans for probes marked "escalation-worthy"; otherwise keep lightweight envelopes.
- Operator UX: default oncall microdash should show <12 panels; everything else collapsed behind a drilldown.

Probe categorization (proposal):
- Canary quick-probe (latency-only, 1s window): runs every 30s, global; emits metric-only (no trace). Targets critical routes (hosted-api text-gen and chat).
- Warmth probe (kv-cache only): runs every 5m per model-family in primary region; emits event + low-sample trace (1/100) for anomalies.
- Throughput probe (throughput check and GPU pressure): runs every 1m on dedicated pools; metric + optional trace if > threshold.
- Regression smoke (semantic quality probe): runs hourly, full trace + prompt payload capture, but limited to dev accounts to avoid PHI.

Sampling & attenuation rules (concrete):
1) Default trace sampling for synthetic probes = 0.5% (0.005) global.
2) If probe latency > p95-slo * 1.5 OR error > 2x baseline for 15m, flip to full-trace capture and mark probe "escalation-worthy" for 2 hours.
3) Any probe from the "regression smoke" family always captures full semantic context but is routed to restricted retention bucket (30 days) and redacted for PHI by default.
4) For warm-start probes: if kv-cache hit-rate difference vs baseline > 5% absolute, increase trace_sample to 5% for 1 hour.

Dashboard decisions (what to show on default oncall panel):
- Keep: global canary quick-probe p50/p95/p99, error-rate, and kv-cache warmth index (simple time series).
- Hide by default: throughput probe per-GPU metrics, semantic quality scores, long tail trace counts. Put these in a collapsed "probes" folder on dashboard.
- Drilldown layout: top row summary (canary latency, error, cache warmth), second row (trace anchors & latest escalations), third row (sampling budget burn-rate and probe health).

Trace anchoring & correlation notes:
- All probes must attach a stable probe_id and route_hint tag so that operator playlists can be reconstructed across microservices.
- Anchor span should be the platform-router span (service=router) with tag probe_id and probe_type. This lets us link a low-sample trace to the relevant route quickly.
- When flipping to full-trace capture, write a short incident marker event to the trace and to the probe-metrics stream (metric probe_escalations_total).

Cost and retention plan (draft numbers):
- Current synthetic trace-ingestion: ~18% of trace budget monthly in EU. Target: reduce to 11% by Q1 2026.
- Strategy: lower sampling floor, add conditional ramp-up on anomalies, move semantic captures to restricted retention.
- Retention tiers: 
  * probe-default: metrics only, traces sampled low, retention 7d full, 30d rollup.
  * probe-escalation: full traces, retention 90d (for complex RCAs) but cost accounted to probe owner cost center.
  * semantic-probe: full traces + payload, restricted retention 30d, review by data-protection before wider rollouts.

Operational checklist (actionable items):
- [ ] Implement trace_sample fallthrough rule in probe runner (owner: Priya). Linked: JIRA-OBS-998.
- [ ] Add probe_id and route_hint tagging to router span (owner: Diego). PR: telemetry#187.
- [ ] Dashboard update: create collapsed probe folder + 12-panel oncall summary (owner: Arielle). Blocker: front-end widget for sampling budget (design required).
- [ ] Cost simulation: run one-week experiment with sampling floor 0.5% -> evaluate ingestion delta (owner: Ethan).
- [ ] Privacy review for semantic probes and retention buckets (owner: Security team).

Open questions / trade-offs to resolve:
- How aggressive can we be with lowering sampling before we lose RCA fidelity for tenant-specific regressions? Proposed mitigation: keep 5% sampling for probe-escalation windows and persist trace anchors.
- Should we treat model-family as a first-class dimension for probe scheduling? Pros: targeted warming. Cons: multiplies probe count by N models. Could do model-family sampling schedule (rotate families every 30m).
- Billing attribution: do we charge probe-escalation retention to the probe owner cost center? Ops likes this, finance wants a formula.

Short-term experiment plan (next 6 weeks):
Week 0: baseline measurement (current probe cost, trace count per region)
Week 1-2: roll sampling floor to 0.5% for all probes in EU (control: US)
Week 3: enable conditional escalation rules in runner; collect escalations and compare RCA success rate vs baseline
Week 4-5: implement dashboard collapsed folder and sampling-budget widget; get oncall feedback
Week 6: decision meeting (go/no-go to make rules global)

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider moving high-frequency metric-only probes into a lighter-weight telemetry sink (in-memory rollup) for 1m aggregates to avoid trace system entirely.
- Add a small synthetic "prompt sampler" to capture failing prompts at 1 per 10k to help quality debugging without large retention.
- Keep an eye on tenant-isolation: when traces include tenant_id, we must ensure PII/PHI redaction precedes retention.

If you're reviewing this doc: focus feedback on the sampling thresholds, probe categories, and dashboard reduced-oncall footprint.

- Meeting notes: confluence://observability/probe-cost-sprint

-- Arielle
